hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with summer crackdown on speeders
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break. He is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said she recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top speed stop was 73 mph. Benning said deputies see a lot of excessive speeding in St. Lucie County.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

Del Toro said he has a family that drives on local roadways and cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones. He said he wants to make St. Lucie County a safer community. Residents say the problem is hard to miss. Ashley, a driver in St. Lucie County, described what she sees on local roads as insane and said nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut people off.

cards.headline: Orlando fentanyl summit draws teens, grieving parents and DEA chief as crisis takes center stage
cards.body:
Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and federal law enforcement at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week, united by a mission to stop fentanyl before it kills more Americans. Students traveled from around the country to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl so they can return home with a message about one of the country's deadliest drug threats. Hannah Kahn, 18, attended after watching a relative's life destroyed by methamphetamine addiction, while 19-year-old Jasmine Figueroa joined as a member of her community anti-drug coalition. Kahn explained that fentanyl often goes unrecognized because it is laced into other drugs rather than being sought out directly. Figueroa urged adults to educate young people openly about drugs, saying it is not a taboo topic and that children will get educated one way or another, so adults might as well be the first to tell them the truth.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and discussed the ongoing threat, stating that the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. Cole said the president has designated Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for law enforcement to target them. The DEA's busiest drug lab has reported finding fentanyl at 16% potency, which a DEA chemist described as high. While deaths from the synthetic opioid are down, tracking how widespread fentanyl has become is nearly impossible in part because of Narcan, an over-the-counter nasal spray that is increasing survival rates.

For parents who have lost children, the summit carries deep personal weight. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023 after buying a Percocet pill that contained fentanyl. Rodriguez said she lives every day with what she didn't know, questioning why she gave her daughter space. Rodriguez said the fight against fentanyl in the U.S. should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on American streets, because the threat has not stopped.

The teen attendees emphasized that prevention comes down to open conversation and making Narcan as common as any household product. Kahn said many people have the stereotype that Narcan is only for responders and EMS, but it should be thought of as a household product, just like Benadryl. The students came with questions and answers about how fentanyl spreads and why young people may not recognize the danger, hoping to take that knowledge back to their communities.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final Sunday as President Trump plans attendance
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a two-year security plan for Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey as President Trump attends the trophy presentation.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs Blue Angels low-altitude Pensacola flyover as safety reviews draw scrutiny
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is encouraging low-altitude military flyovers after a Blue Angels jet buzzed a crowded Pensacola beach this week, sending chairs and tents flying.
cards.body:
Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's demonstration squadron, the Blue Angels, flying so low over a crowded beach in Pensacola on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. Then on Thursday morning, a host of Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote "Carry on Patriots" on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing people on a beach taking photos of a Blue Angels jet, with the words "Freedom" and "It's okay to love America."

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration political appointee, said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. His social media post was retweeted by Hegseth. Cao's post said Thursday that the Blue Angels conducted a flight debrief. Navy officials would not say if that debrief, typically a routine occurrence after every flight, was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. It is at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that, while often popular with the crowds experiencing them, have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of the safety investigations. Jeff Guzzetti, an aviation safety consultant who used to investigate crashes for both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking to him as an aviation safety professional that the top leaders of the military would excuse this type of reckless behavior. He said a cavalier attitude like that can only lead to accidents in his view.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England with late goals to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two goals in the final five minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals Wednesday, advancing to face Spain in Sunday's final.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. Anthony Gordon scored the opening goal for England in the 55th minute. Messi fed the ball to Fernandez to sweep in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner. Martinez said he told Alexis Mac Allister that he was going to come on and win it. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as wave after wave of Argentina attacks came. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team showed collectiveness, brotherhood, and the fight to the very end. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk, played with more rhythm, and played with the feeling that they have nothing to lose anymore, which freed them up and held England back. The loss marks the third time England has fallen in the World Cup semifinals after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, the staff, and the fans.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence for game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball restricted iPad usage in dugouts starting Wednesday night to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to help make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night when the second half of the season began. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and previously included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. In many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches, according to MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant general managers and video coordinators.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. MLB said instituting the prohibition beginning with the second half of the season was intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead time to make any necessary adjustments.

MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi bathed Spain's Lamine Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot before Sunday's World Cup final
cards.teaser: Photographer Joan Monfort's 2007 photos of teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal have gone viral before Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a baby boy named Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. Messi, then playing for Barcelona, was paired with the infant who would become a star for Barcelona some 15 years later. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble, and Yamal erupted at the club two years later. The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey, when Argentina plays Spain.

Monfort, 58, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title. Monfort said interest in his photos has skyrocketed with the World Cup final looming, and the fact that the final is in the United States has given it extra push. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets, while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. Monfort said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: World Cup final tickets cost more than average monthly US household income
cards.teaser: The cheapest ticket for Sunday's World Cup final on resale sites is about $7,700, nearly identical to what the median U.S. household earns in an entire month.
cards.body:
The cheapest ticket on resale sites currently for sale for the World Cup final is about $7,700. That's nearly identical to what the median U.S. household earns in an entire month. If you want to sit in the lower bowl of the stadium, be prepared to spend at least $10,000.

FIFA has faced criticism over the high ticket prices, which it says reflect strong global demand. Tickets for the third-place game in Miami start at about $700. According to Forbes, this year's World Cup Final could end up being the most expensive sports ticket in U.S. history. The final is Sunday.

cards.headline: World Cup boosts beer sales 14 percent in U.S. host cities during tournament
cards.teaser: Beer sales in bars, restaurants, stadiums and other venues rose 14 percent in U.S. host cities during the first four weeks of the World Cup compared to the same period last year.
cards.body:
In the first four weeks of the tournament, beer sales in bars, restaurants, stadiums and other venues rose 14 percent in U.S. host cities compared to the same period last year, according to the Beer Institute. The bump extended beyond host cities, with sales up 4 percent nationally. Bars in Boston reported needing emergency deliveries to keep taps from running dry on some game days. Fans downed a total of 290,000 stadium beers during the six matches in Philadelphia, FIFA organizers said.

Jim Koch, the brewer, founder and CEO of the Boston Beer Co., which makes Samuel Adams and other brands, said the company had to make two emergency deliveries to its Sam Adams Boston Taproom on the first day that Scotland's fans were in town. At one point, the bar was pouring a Sam Adams Boston Lager every 12 seconds. Koch said he did not see a single person on their phone, noting they had a beer in their hand and were talking to each other. Beer consumption has fallen steadily for a decade in the U.S., according to the Brewers Association, a trade group for craft brewers. Many consumers are cutting back on alcohol for health reasons. Last year was the first time in Gallup's polling that a majority of Americans, 53 percent, said drinking one or two drinks a day was bad for one's health.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast gymnasts from Flip City qualify for Junior Olympics after top 15 national finish
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month, qualifying them for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as one unit on the national stage throughout what Head Coach Candice Lazuka described as a strong season. The team competed locally, traveled, and advanced to states and regionals before their national competition.

At AAU Nationals, the gymnasts came close to a perfect score, earning a 9.9. Lazuka said it is hard to get a perfect 10. Each gymnast came to the sport through different paths. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really gymnastics but the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by all the gymnasts she saw on YouTube and how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves it because she learns new things. Looking ahead to the Junior Olympics, Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she is going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings as happy and exciting at the same time.

hero.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10 and announces Wild Night Out adults-only events
hero.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo extended its Kids Free promotion and announced the return of its Wild Night Out series on the last Saturdays of July, August and September.
hero.body:
Palm Beach Zoo extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, according to zoo officials. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, shared the updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters.

Palm Beach Zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include Paws & Santa Claus in July, Tails & Touchdowns in August and Decades After Dark in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. Zoo officials said a previous Wild Night Out event in June featured line dancing lessons led by Dance Till Dawn. July's event will also serve as an early preview of this year's Zoo Lights celebration. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to 1,250 children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is providing thousands of free meals to children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program while school is out for the summer.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children. Food Bank CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county. The organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone.

The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed. Food Bank leaders said the meals are distributed through partner locations across Palm Beach County to help families facing food insecurity during the summer. The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach.

cards.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa discounts for July and August
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched a mobile-exclusive Wellness Pass offering free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness promotions from participating businesses.
cards.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is encouraging residents and visitors to prioritize health and self-care this summer through a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. According to the DDA, the mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach.

The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is participating with wellness-related services and promotions. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida. Many consumers are seeking affordable ways to stay active, reduce stress and support local businesses during the summer months. More information and a complete list of participating offers can be found on the DDA website.

cards.headline: Gulf and Atlantic tropical disturbances carry low odds of development this week
cards.teaser: Tropical disturbances in both the Gulf of Mexico and Atlantic Ocean have low chances of development this week, according to forecasters.
cards.body:
The National Hurricane Center is monitoring tropical disturbances in both the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean. Forecasters have assessed both systems as having low odds of development over the coming days. While the disturbances are being tracked, no immediate tropical formation is expected.

The monitoring comes as Florida enters the height of the Atlantic hurricane season. Residents and officials across the state continue to watch weather patterns for any changes that could affect coastal and inland areas. The low development odds provide some relief as communities prepare for the possibility of tropical weather throughout the season.

hero.headline: Murray Middle School demolition begins in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
hero.teaser: Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, starting a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton.
hero.body:
Demolition is underway at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The demolition phase alone carries a price tag of $3.3 million, though officials have not yet finalized the total cost for the entire project. The reconstruction will be funded through a combination of local capital improvement funds, sales tax revenue, and Public Education Capital Outlay.

The project extends beyond simply rebuilding what was lost in the storm. According to Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, Murray Middle School was already scheduled to receive construction work including a new administration area, a new media center, and a brand new art lab. When Hurricane Milton's tornadoes destroyed buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to incorporate reconstruction of those structures into the planned improvements. The comprehensive project will also include a complete overhaul of the school's parking lot.

Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms are continuing their education in portable classrooms while construction proceeds. The school district has emphasized that parents can be assured their children will remain safe during the construction period. Barriers have already been installed around the work zone to prevent students from entering the construction areas and to maintain a secure learning environment for those still on campus.

The Martin County School District hopes to complete all renovations by December 2027. The extended timeline reflects the scope of work needed to both repair tornado damage and complete the previously planned facility improvements. By combining the storm recovery effort with already scheduled upgrades, the district is working to transform the campus challenges into an opportunity for comprehensive modernization that will serve students for years to come.

Benning said she recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top speed stop was 73 mph. Benning said deputies see a lot of excessive speeding in St. Lucie County.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

Del Toro said he has a family that drives on local roadways and cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones. He said he wants to make St. Lucie County a safer community. Residents say the problem is hard to miss. Ashley, a driver in St. Lucie County, described what she sees on local roads as insane and said nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut people off.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman turns $20 scratch-off into $5 million lottery jackpot
cards.teaser: Maria Duran, 57, claimed a $5 million top prize from the Florida Lottery after purchasing her winning ticket at a Fort Pierce convenience store.
cards.body: Florida Lottery officials announced Friday that Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, turning $20 into $5 million. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138. Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90, but the chance of winning $5 million playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135.

hero.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to JFK Airport in September
hero.teaser: JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December.
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue said in a statement that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route and has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast.

The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment to local officials and residents who had hoped the direct connection would strengthen ties between the two regions. The discontinuation of the JFK route after such a short period highlights the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining air service to major hubs. While JetBlue's Boston service will continue to provide some connectivity for Vero Beach travelers, the loss of direct access to JFK eliminates what many saw as a crucial link to the New York metropolitan area.

The airline has not indicated whether it might reconsider the route in the future or explore other destinations from Vero Beach Regional Airport. The route had been viewed as important infrastructure for the region when it first began operations, with hopes that convenient access to JFK would help strengthen economic and personal connections between the Treasure Coast and the New York metropolitan area. The short lifespan of the route underscores the difficulties regional airports encounter when trying to establish and maintain service to major transportation hubs.
